reuse.why: Most month-wide actions share the new category selector and existing budget helpers, but copyPreviousMonth independently implements the same eligibility policy.

duplication.why: Repeated category queries are consolidated, but exclusions remain duplicated between SQL selection and copyPreviousMonth, and the new action repeats the income eligibility guard.

placement.why: Selection and budget mutation remain in budget/actions.ts, with method registration and undo wrapping in budget/app.ts.

scope.why: The changes focus on the requested budget actions, apart from removing an income-category fixture from an existing copyUntilYearEnd test.

maintainability.why: The shared selector improves ownership, but maintaining equivalent exclusion rules in SQL and JavaScript invites drift, and its name no longer describes its full policy.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth bypasses getVisibleCategoriesWithoutTemplates and applies equivalent exclusions using getBudgetData flags.

disguised_duplication.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: the selector's WHERE predicates are reshaped into has_template/is_fixed SQL projections and a JavaScript exclusion condition for copyPreviousMonth.

abstraction_drift.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: the shared selector gains includeHiddenCategories and its conditional hidden-filter bypass, while copyPreviousMonth maintains a separate implementation of the evolving eligibility policy.
